reason: The cited evidence shows Hf improves oxidation resistance in a different HEA system (E1) and affects coating morphology in CoCrFeNiHfx (E2), but neither supports the key premises that pre-coating FeCoNiCrAl feedstock with Hf will form an in-situ HfO2 layer during spraying, reduce in-flight oxidation, or increase coating thickness to ~120 μm. The 120 μm value is from a bulk Hf-coated composite, not a thermal-sprayed bond coat, and the mechanism of enhanced cohesion is unsupported.
premises: A thin Hf-rich coating on feedstock can be applied uniformly (e.g., via PVD).
The Hf coating will preferentially oxidize during thermal spray to form a protective HfO2 layer.
This HfO2 layer will reduce in-flight oxidation of the underlying FeCoNiCrAl.
Reduced oxidation will enhance particle cohesion and deposition efficiency, yielding a thicker coating.
The resulting coating thickness will be significantly greater (~120 μm) than the untreated baseline.
